we have identified dihydropyirmidinase-like protein 3 (DPYSL3) as a novel protein highly expressed in human PDAC and that DPYSL3 regulates pancreatic cancer cell adhesion, migration, and metastasis by interacting with and stabilizing the focal adhesion complex.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified a novel pancreatic ductal adenocrinicoma-associated protein, dihyropyrimidinase 3, by using combined proteomic approaches and demonstrated that the expression of the protein was associated with the metastasis and poor survival of the patients, and the protein promoted pancreatic cancer cell adhesion, migration, and metastasis through interaction with and stabilization of the focal adhesion complex consisting Ezrin and cSrc, and that the interaction promoted activation of the focal adhension complex.

we identified a protein, Dihydropyrimidase-like 3 (DPYSL3) as a novel biomarker for pancreatic ductal adenacarcinoma (PDAC), which is highly expressed in PDAC tissues and pancreatic cancer cell lines, using a proteomic approach.
the combined proteomics approach, iTRAQ and MRM, is a powerful tool for identifying the molecular mechanism of pancreatic cancer progression and the potential biomarkers for pancreatic cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of proteomic technologies and in vitro and in vivo functional assays can be a powerful approach to identify novel key players that regulate pancreatic cancer metastasis.
the combined proteomic approach is a powerful tool to identify key players in pancreatic cancer tumorigenesis.
we identified DPYSL3, a protein that is overexpressed in pancreatic cancer, as a novel regulator of cancer cell adhesion, migration and metastasis.
